cohort: Pregnant women who had previously undergone MBS (n=79) compared to age and pre-pregnancy BMI-matched controls who had not undergone surgery (n=79)
finding: Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) was associated with a lower prevalence of gestational diabetes and lower birth weight compared to non-operated women with similar age and BMI.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in the mode of delivery between the MBS group and the control group.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight observed in the MBS group compared to controls (2953.67 ± 489.51 g vs. 3229.11 ± 476.21 g; p < 0.01)
